question.text: Regarding entry loads in mutual funds, which of the following statements is correct?

answer.text: Entry loads have been prohibited by SEBI
Entry loads of up to 2.25% are permitted for equity schemes
Entry loads are charged only for closed-ended schemes
Entry loads are optional and decided by the AMC for each scheme

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI has prohibited entry loads in mutual funds. Currently, only exit loads are permitted, and these are linked to the holding period of the investor. The Trap: Any option suggesting that entry loads are permitted — whether for equity schemes, closed-ended schemes, or at the discretion of the AMC — is incorrect. The prohibition applies across scheme types. Note: Exit loads, where charged, must be credited back to the scheme and not retained by the AMC, subject to the limits prescribed by SEBI.
